text: Bisection, minimization and boundary testing share one move. What is it?
choices: Each observation eliminates a fraction of the possibilities rather than testing one candidate
Each works only on small programs
Each tests candidates one at a time
explanation: Testing candidates one by one is linear; halving is logarithmic. The difference is between an afternoon and five minutes, and it is available in almost every debugging situation — which is why it is worth making explicit rather than discovering by accident.
